# [STORY] As a Presenter, I want a local Cloudflare Tunnel option so that I can expose my local or Minikube backend to Vercel

## User Story
**As a** Presenter / Developer
**I want** a 1-command local Cloudflare Tunnel deployment for Docker and Minikube
**So that** I can expose my locally running microservices stack to the Vercel-deployed frontend via public HTTPS with zero cloud cost and zero VM provisioning

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the local stack running (Docker Compose or Minikube, gateway reachable at `http://localhost:8080`), when running `./gradlew startTunnel`, then a `cloudflared` container launches and its logs yield a public HTTPS URL (`test_tunnel_scripts.TunnelScriptTest.test_start_tunnel_publishes_the_extracted_public_url`)
- [x] Given a Minikube cluster, when checking `infrastructure/kubernetes/overlays/local/cloudflare-tunnel.yaml`, then it is a correctly-targeted `cloudflared` Deployment manifest — not wired into `kustomization.yaml` or any script, since Minikube exposure goes through the same `start-tunnel.sh` as Compose once the gateway answers on `localhost:8080` (`test_tunnel_manifests.KubernetesTunnelManifestTest`); rescoped, see Notes
- [x] Given an active tunnel, when the URL is generated, then it is published to `infrastructure/tunnel-url.txt` and the deployed frontend's `resolveApiUrl()` falls back to it automatically (`test_tunnel_scripts.TunnelScriptTest.test_start_tunnel_publishes_the_extracted_public_url`, `apiUrl.test.js`'s "falls back to the published tunnel URL when both cloud health checks fail and the tunnel is healthy")
- [x] Given someone wants to expose a local backend, when they read `README.md`'s "Local Stack + Tunnel" row or `docs/guides/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`, then `startTunnel`/`stopTunnel` and the `tunnel-url.txt` auto-sync are documented there, not in an Admin UI — `DeployControl.jsx` was deleted under ADR-015 (`README.md:199-217`, `docs/guides/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md:103-110`)

## Definition of Ready
